claims.text: First: which study is it? Noncontrast CT: used to detect lung nodules
claims.quote: To detect acute hemorrhage in the brain, urinary calculi, and lung nodules

claims.text: IV contrast: used to assess the vessels when pulmonary embolism, aortic aneurysm or aortic dissection is suspected
claims.quote: To assess the vascular system, as when pulmonary embolism, aortic aneurysm, or aortic dissection is suspected

claims.text: CT angiography (CTA, CT-PA): thin slices taken right after a rapid IV contrast bolus, while the contrast fills the arteries and veins
claims.quote: After a rapid bolus injection of IV contrast, thin-slice images are rapidly taken as the contrast opacifies arteries and veins.

claims.text: Pulmonary arteries (CT-PA) Emboli show as filling defects inside the contrast-filled pulmonary arteries
claims.quote: The images show bilateral pulmonary embolism on chest computed tomographic angiography. The arrows point to the filling defects (emboli).

claims.text: CT angiography is least sensitive for emboli in subsegmental vessels
claims.quote: Sensitivity of CT angiography is lowest for emboli in subsegmental vessels

claims.text: Then the heart: right ventricle size and contrast reflux into the hepatic veins show how severe the PE is
claims.quote: as well as severity of PE (for example by the size of the right ventricle or the reflux into the hepatic veins)

claims.text: Lungs Look at the lungs for another cause, such as pneumonia instead of PE
claims.quote: It can also give more information about other lung pathology (eg, demonstration of pneumonia rather than PE as a cause of hypoxia or pleuritic chest pain)

claims.text: Nodules: calcification suggests a benign nodule, especially central, concentric or popcorn calcification
claims.quote: Calcification suggests nonmalignant disease, particularly if it is central (tuberculoma, histoplasmoma), concentric (healed histoplasmosis), or in a popcorn configuration (hamartoma).

claims.text: Compare with old images: a nodule that has not grown in 2 years or more suggests a benign cause
claims.quote: A lesion that has not enlarged in ≥ 2 years suggests a benign etiology.

claims.text: CT can tell a lung opacity from a pleural one
claims.quote: CT can also distinguish pulmonary from pleural radiopacities.
